童.meaning: The <part>farm</part>'s new scarecrow can't <part>stand</part> still. It giggles when crows land, sneaks apples from the barrels and swaps its hat with the goat's. One evening it climbs down and runs in for dinner. It was a mischievous <kanji>juvenile</kanji> in a straw hat all along.
童.on: In the kitchen he shapes a lump of bread <sound>dough</sound> into a crow.
童.kun: His mum hands him <sound>wa</sound>sabi peas and a bowl of <sound>ra</sound>men, then sends him to <sound>be</sound>d.

輝.meaning: An <part>army</part> marches out at dawn, but the general has made the soldiers polish their helmets so hard that the first <part>ray</part> of sun bounces off every one. The enemy is dazzled, squints, and goes home for sunglasses. The battle is won by pure <kanji>radiance</kanji>.
輝.on: The general's only medal is a polished brass <sound>key</sound>.
輝.kun: Back at camp the cook serves <sound>car</sound>p with <sound>gar</sound>lic, and the soldiers knit helmet covers from <sound>ya</sound>rn.

飼.meaning: A film <part>director</part> needs a wild raccoon for her movie. Each day she leaves a bowl of <part>food</part> a little closer to the set, until one morning the raccoon is sitting in her chair, wearing her cap and shouting 'Cut!' She meant to <kanji>domesticate</kanji> it, not hire it.
飼.on: Now it naps behind her desk on a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld.
飼.kun: She also keeps a pond <sound>car</sound>p, which wants its own trailer.

湾.meaning: A <part>jellyfish</part> wants a quiet place to float, so it draws a <part>bow</part> and shoots an arrow at the coast. The cliffs bend inward like the curve of the bow, and the sea rushes in, <part>water drops</part> spraying. Now it has its own calm <kanji>gulf</kanji>.
湾.on: The fish say it <sound>won</sound> the prize for the prettiest coast.
湾.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l moves into its <sound>ree</sound>f and lays an <sound>e</sound>gg there.

黙.meaning: A library hires a big <part>black</part> <part>dog</part> as its night guard. It never barks: when a burglar creeps in, it just stares from the dark shelves with two glowing eyes until he tiptoes out again. The librarian loves its perfect <kanji>silence</kanji>.
黙.on: It pads between the shelves in soft <sound>moc</sound>casin slippers.
黙.kun: Even the <sound>du</sound>ck in the pond and its <sound>ma</sound>ma stop quacking when it walks past.

煮.meaning: <part>Someone</part> on a camping trip has lost her kettle, so she fills her own rubber boot with water and sets it on the <part>hot coals</part>. Soon it bubbles, steams and smells faintly of socks. She makes tea anyway: water is water once you <kanji>boil</kanji> it.
煮.on: She fans the coals with a <sound>shu</sound>ttlecock to make it bubble faster.
煮.kun: Then she stirs the boot with a knitting <sound>nee</sound>dle.

祈.meaning: In thick fog, a lumberjack swings his <part>axe</part> at what he thinks is a tree. It's a <part>lamppost</part>, and the axe sticks fast. He tugs, then kneels under the glowing lamp, hands together, begging it to let go before the council finds out. All night, he can only <kanji>pray</kanji>.
祈.on: At dawn a cleaner opens a little door in the post with a <sound>key</sound>, and the axe drops out.
祈.kun: To say thanks, he leaves the lamp a smoked <sound>ee</sound>l and a handwritten <sound>no</sound>te.
